text:
maria: FYI — during the US-west promo window we saw a weird pattern: overall GPU utilization ~45% but request queue depth climbed and p95 latency hit 1.8s for short chat requests. link: https://grafana.redwood/links/abc123
aj: ugh, so burst pool wasn't helping even though there was capacity?
hitoshi: can you paste the autoscaler events? suspect backoff hysteresis kept us from spinning up extra nodes in time
autoscale-bot: Event: burst-request-triggered -> attempted-scale +6 gpus; ScaleAction delayed by 00:01:20 due to recent-scale-backoff policy
samira: quick note — network egress showed occasional spiky retransmits on a subset of nodes in us-west-2 around the same time (netconn errors). might've increased token-expansion latency
maria: here's the relevant snippet from the autoscaler config we currently use:
```
burst:
  max_extra_gpus: 200
  per_region_cap: 40
  holdback_ratio: 0.12
  scale_backoff: 80s
  min_steady: 180
```
aj: holdback_ratio 0.12 seems high for promos where traffic bursts quickly. might buy stability but hurts headroom
hitoshi:Agreed. Also the scale_backoff of 80s + our reserve window (3m) meant we missed ~2 minutes of traffic while waiting.
samira: The network spikes could make individual inferences slower which increases queue depth even if avg GPU load looks low. so autoscaler sees low avg utilization and doesn't react
maria: TL;DR: autoscaler logic needs to consider queue depth + short-term P90 latency as a second signal, not just GPU utilization
aj: doable. propose: add quick-path that if queue_depth > 200 for 30s OR p90_lat > 1s then allow temporary burst upto per_region_cap irrespective of holdback (but with stricter rollout cooldown)
hitoshi: also: add network health gating — if TCP retransmit rate > threshold, reduce burst multiplier since extra nodes won't help network congestion
samira: cost note: increasing burst caps will raise committed GPU-hours during promo windows. but losing requests = bad UX and also lost revenue. need to show tradeoff numbers
maria: Samira can you run a 7-day sim comparing current policy vs proposed quick-path? aim to show expected extra GPU-hours and p95 latency improvement
samira: on it. rough numbers I'll attach in a follow-up.
aj: implementation plan:
- short-term: tweak holdback_ratio -> 0.06 and scale_backoff -> 40s in us-west-2 for promo window (canary to 10% of traffic)
- mid-term: add queue_depth & p90 trigger into autoscaler decision logic
- mid-term: add network gating heuristic
- runbook: if p95 stays >2s after scale, rollback burst rule and open incident
hitoshi: for the code change, I can add a heuristic inside scorer: if queue_depth_score >= 0.6 || p90_score >= 0.6 -> force-allow-burst flag. Simple boolean for first rollout.
maria: thanks. @ops-bot can you schedule a controlled canary for today 2100 UTC, target 10% of us-west traffic, and apply holdback_ratio 0.06 for 40m?
ops-bot: Canary scheduled: 2025-11-04T21:00:00Z -> 40m window. Policy applied to target cluster pool 'uw2-promo-canary'
aj: good. also let's add a short alert in the console for queue_depth p90 so on-call sees it sooner
samira: opened a quick PR with sim results (draft) and cost delta: expected +0.9% GPU-hours over 24h promos, p95 latency improvement ~35% in test harness
hitoshi: code PR coming in ~2 hours. will put feature flag behind rollout:flag.autoscaler.queue_trigger
maria: nice. after the canary we meet 30m post-mortem, collect traces and decide whether to extend to 100% in region
aj: one more thought — consider transient caching (KV prefix caching) to reduce backend work during promos; might reduce need for large bursts
samira: added to backlog: RFC for promo caching + autoscaler interplay
maria: great. thanks everyone — keep thread updates short. I'll post the post-canary notes here. :thumbsup:
